capture.final_message:
Use the neighborhood characterization of semicontinuity by strict order rays.

For the first conjunct, fix \(a<f(x)\). The upper ray \((a,\infty)\) is an open neighborhood of \(f(x)\) in the order topology. `ContinuousWithinAt` pulls it back to an eventual condition on \(s\), giving \(a<f(y)\) near \(x\), exactly lower semicontinuity within \(s\).

For the second, fix \(b>f(x)+g(x)\). Continuity and monotonicity of addition make
\[
\{(u,v)\mid u+v<b\}
\]
an open downward-closed neighborhood of \((f(x),g(x))\). Choose downward open neighborhoods \(U\ni f(x)\) and \(V\ni g(x)\) with \(U\times V\) inside this set. Upper semicontinuity of \(f\) and \(g\) gives \(f(z)\in U\) and \(g(z)\in V\) eventually; intersecting these eventual conditions yields \(f(z)+g(z)<b\). This is the desired upper semicontinuity of the sum.

The essential ingredients are the order topology, order-preservation of addition, and continuity of addition; subtraction or a density assumption is unnecessary.
